name: Read a decimal to thousandths
description: Student can read a decimal number with up to three decimal places.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown 4.205, the student reads 'four and two hundred and five thousandths'.
commonError: Student reads the decimal part as a whole number, saying 'four point two hundred and five'.
checkpointTask: Show decimals to thousandths. Ask the student to read each.

name: Compare two decimals
description: Student can compare two decimals including numbers greater than one.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 3.7 is greater than 3.07.
commonError: Student says the decimal with more digits is larger, calling 3.07 bigger than 3.7.
checkpointTask: Give pairs of decimals. Ask the student which is larger and how they know.

name: Order decimals
description: Student can order a set of decimals from smallest to largest.
exampleOfSuccess: Given 0.5, 0.45, 0.405, the student orders 0.405, 0.45, 0.5.
commonError: Student orders by the length of the decimal rather than the value.
checkpointTask: Give several decimals. Ask the student to order them.

name: Locate a decimal on a number line
description: Student can locate a decimal on a number line.
exampleOfSuccess: The student marks 2.6 between 2 and 3, six tenths along.
commonError: Student places decimals without using equal intervals.
checkpointTask: Give a number line. Ask the student to mark several decimals.

name: Rename a decimal
description: Student can rename a decimal to help with mental computation.
exampleOfSuccess: The student renames 1.5 as 15 tenths.
commonError: Student cannot rename across place values.
checkpointTask: Pose decimals. Ask the student to rename each a different way.

name: List the factors of a number
description: Student can list the factors of a natural number.
exampleOfSuccess: For 12, the student lists 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
commonError: Student lists multiples instead of factors, or misses a factor pair.
checkpointTask: Give numbers. Ask the student to list all the factors of each.

name: Express a number as a product of factors
description: Student can express a natural number as a product of its factors.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes 24 as 4 x 6 and as 2 x 2 x 2 x 3.
commonError: Student gives a product that does not equal the number.
checkpointTask: Give numbers. Ask the student to write each as a product of factors.

name: Identify multiples
description: Student can identify the multiples of a number.
exampleOfSuccess: The student lists 6, 12, 18, 24 as multiples of 6.
commonError: Student lists factors instead of multiples.
checkpointTask: Give a number. Ask the student to list its first several multiples.

name: Use a divisibility test
description: Student can use a divisibility test to check if a number is divisible by another.
exampleOfSuccess: The student uses the digit-sum rule to show 132 is divisible by 3.
commonError: Student applies the wrong rule, or applies the rule incorrectly.
checkpointTask: Give numbers and divisors. Ask the student to test divisibility.

name: Determine if one number divides another
description: Student can determine whether one number is divisible by another and justify it.
exampleOfSuccess: The student shows 96 is divisible by 8 because 8 x 12 = 96.
commonError: Student guesses without testing or justifying.
checkpointTask: Pose divisibility questions. Ask the student to decide and justify each.

name: Compare fractions with the same denominator
description: Student can compare fractions with the same denominator.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 5/8 is greater than 3/8.
commonError: Student compares the denominators instead of the numerators.
checkpointTask: Give same-denominator fractions. Ask the student which is larger.

name: Compare fractions with related denominators
description: Student can compare fractions with related denominators using equivalence.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 2/3 is greater than 1/2 by finding sixths.
commonError: Student compares numerators or denominators directly without finding equivalents.
checkpointTask: Give related-denominator fractions. Ask the student which is larger.

name: Order fractions
description: Student can order a set of fractions with related denominators.
exampleOfSuccess: The student orders 1/2, 3/4, 2/3 correctly using a common denominator.
commonError: Student orders by numerator or denominator alone.
checkpointTask: Give several fractions. Ask the student to order them.

name: Locate fractions on a number line
description: Student can locate fractions and mixed numerals on a number line.
exampleOfSuccess: The student marks 1 and 1/4 and 3/4 in the right places.
commonError: Student spaces the fractions unequally or misplaces the mixed numeral.
checkpointTask: Give a number line. Ask the student to mark several fractions and mixed numerals.

name: Convert between mixed and improper fractions
description: Student can convert between mixed numerals and improper fractions to help compare.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes 2 and 1/3 as 7/3 to compare it with 5/3.
commonError: Student converts incorrectly, mishandling the whole number.
checkpointTask: Give mixed and improper fractions. Ask the student to convert and compare.

name: Recognise 100% as the whole
description: Student can recognise that 100% represents one complete whole.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 100% of a pizza is the whole pizza.
commonError: Student treats 100% as a quantity unrelated to the whole.
checkpointTask: Pose situations. Ask the student what 100% of each means.

name: Connect a percentage to a fraction
description: Student can connect a common percentage to its fraction equivalent.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 25% is the same as 1/4.
commonError: Student writes 25% as 1/25.
checkpointTask: Give common percentages. Ask the student for the fraction equivalent of each.

name: Connect a percentage to a decimal
description: Student can connect a common percentage to its decimal equivalent.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 50% is the same as 0.5.
commonError: Student writes 50% as 50.0 or 0.05.
checkpointTask: Give common percentages. Ask the student for the decimal equivalent of each.

name: Use percentages to compare
description: Student can use percentages to compare relative sizes.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says scoring 80% is better than 7 out of 10 (70%).
commonError: Student compares the raw numbers without converting to a common base.
checkpointTask: Pose comparisons. Ask the student to use percentages to decide.

name: Add fractions with the same denominator
description: Student can add fractions with the same denominator.
exampleOfSuccess: The student adds 2/5 and 1/5 to get 3/5.
commonError: Student adds the denominators as well, giving 3/10.
checkpointTask: Pose same-denominator additions. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Subtract fractions with the same denominator
description: Student can subtract fractions with the same denominator.
exampleOfSuccess: The student works 5/6 minus 2/6 to get 3/6.
commonError: Student subtracts the denominators too.
checkpointTask: Pose same-denominator subtractions. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Add fractions with related denominators
description: Student can add fractions with related denominators by finding equivalents.
exampleOfSuccess: For 1/2 plus 1/4, the student rewrites 1/2 as 2/4 to get 3/4.
commonError: Student adds without making the denominators the same.
checkpointTask: Pose related-denominator additions. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Solve a fraction problem
description: Student can solve a practical problem involving adding or subtracting fractions.
exampleOfSuccess: For a recipe needing 1/2 and 1/4 cups, the student finds 3/4 of a cup total.
commonError: Student adds the numbers without treating them as fractions.
checkpointTask: Pose practical fraction problems. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Multiply a larger number by a single digit
description: Student can multiply a three-digit number by a single digit.
exampleOfSuccess: For 253 x 4, the student partitions and finds 1012.
commonError: Student forgets to regroup, or multiplies only part of the number.
checkpointTask: Pose larger-by-single-digit multiplications. Ask the student to solve.

name: Multiply by a two-digit number
description: Student can multiply a larger number by a two-digit number using partitioning or an area model.
exampleOfSuccess: For 36 x 24, the student splits into parts to find 864.
commonError: Student multiplies by only one digit of the two-digit number.
checkpointTask: Pose two-digit multiplications. Ask the student to solve using an area model.

name: Use a factor or doubling strategy
description: Student can use factors or doubling to multiply efficiently.
exampleOfSuccess: For 253 x 4, the student doubles twice instead of multiplying by 4 directly.
commonError: Student doubles the wrong number of times or once only.
checkpointTask: Pose multiplications suited to doubling or factors. Ask the student to solve efficiently.

name: Check the reasonableness of a product
description: Student can check whether a product is reasonable using estimation.
exampleOfSuccess: For 253 x 4, the student estimates 250 x 4 = 1000 and sees 1012 is reasonable.
commonError: Student accepts an unreasonable product without checking.
checkpointTask: Give answered multiplications. Ask the student to estimate and judge each.

name: Solve a division with an efficient strategy
description: Student can solve a division problem using an efficient strategy.
exampleOfSuccess: For 156 divided by 4, the student uses known facts to find 39.
commonError: Student has no strategy for larger divisions.
checkpointTask: Pose division problems. Ask the student to solve using an efficient strategy.

name: Interpret a remainder in context
description: Student can interpret a remainder according to the context of a problem.
exampleOfSuccess: For '29 students in cars of 4', the student says 8 cars are needed.
commonError: Student gives the remainder as the answer without interpreting the context.
checkpointTask: Pose division problems with remainders. Ask the student what the remainder means.

name: Express a remainder as a fraction or decimal
description: Student can express a remainder as a fraction or decimal where appropriate.
exampleOfSuccess: For 13 divided by 4, the student gives 3 and 1/4 or 3.25.
commonError: Student writes the remainder as a whole number regardless of context.
checkpointTask: Pose divisions that do not divide evenly. Ask the student to express the result suitably.

name: Solve a practical division problem
description: Student can solve a practical division problem and express the result suitably.
exampleOfSuccess: Sharing $50 among 4, the student finds $12.50 each.
commonError: Student ignores the context when deciding how to express the result.
checkpointTask: Pose practical division problems. Ask the student to solve and express each result.

name: Round to estimate a calculation
description: Student can round numbers appropriately to estimate a calculation.
exampleOfSuccess: For 412 x 6, the student estimates 400 x 6 = 2400.
commonError: Student rounds to a place that makes the estimate unhelpful.
checkpointTask: Pose calculations. Ask the student to round and estimate each.

name: Decide if an exact or estimated answer is needed
description: Student can decide whether a problem needs an exact answer or an estimate.
exampleOfSuccess: For 'is $50 enough', the student estimates rather than calculating exactly.
commonError: Student always calculates exactly even when an estimate would do.
checkpointTask: Pose problems. Ask the student whether each needs an exact answer or an estimate.

name: Check a financial calculation
description: Student can use estimation to check a financial calculation.
exampleOfSuccess: The student estimates a shopping total to check the till receipt is about right.
commonError: Student does not check, or cannot estimate to compare.
checkpointTask: Give a financial calculation and result. Ask the student to estimate and judge it.

name: Explain why an answer is reasonable
description: Student can explain the reasoning behind judging an answer reasonable.
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains the estimate is close to the answer, so it is reasonable.
commonError: Student judges reasonableness with no reasoning.
checkpointTask: After a check, ask the student to explain why the answer is or is not reasonable.

name: Choose operations for a practical problem
description: Student can choose the operations needed for a multi-step practical problem.
exampleOfSuccess: For a two-step problem, the student chooses multiplication then subtraction.
commonError: Student uses one operation for a problem that needs two.
checkpointTask: Pose multi-step problems. Ask the student which operations each needs.

name: Model a multi-step problem
description: Student can model and solve a multi-step practical problem.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes and solves the steps for a problem in order.
commonError: Student solves only one step, or combines steps incorrectly.
checkpointTask: Pose multi-step problems. Ask the student to model and solve each.

name: Model a budget
description: Student can model a practical financial problem such as a budget.
exampleOfSuccess: For a class fundraiser, the student builds a budget of costs and income.
commonError: Student leaves out a cost or does not compare income to costs.
checkpointTask: Pose a budgeting problem. Ask the student to model and solve it.

name: Interpret and communicate the solution
description: Student can interpret and communicate the solution in terms of the situation.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says the fundraiser makes a $40 profit, so the plan works.
commonError: Student gives a number without relating it to the situation.
checkpointTask: After a problem, ask the student what the answer means for the situation.

name: Follow an algorithm for factors or multiples
description: Student can follow an algorithm to find factors, multiples or divisibility.
exampleOfSuccess: Following an algorithm, the student lists the factors of 36.
commonError: Student skips a step or stops early.
checkpointTask: Give an algorithm for factors or multiples. Ask the student to follow it.

name: Create an algorithm for divisibility
description: Student can create an algorithm to test divisibility or generate multiples.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes steps to test whether a number is divisible by 4.
commonError: Student writes steps that are unclear or give the wrong result.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to write an algorithm to test a divisibility rule.

name: Use a spreadsheet to generate a pattern
description: Student can use a spreadsheet and the fill-down function to generate a number pattern.
exampleOfSuccess: The student uses a multiplication formula and fill-down to list multiples.
commonError: Student enters values by hand or writes a formula that does not fill correctly.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to use a spreadsheet to generate multiples of a number.

name: Describe an emerging pattern
description: Student can describe the patterns that emerge, such as common multiples or factors.
exampleOfSuccess: The student identifies the lowest common multiple of two numbers from the lists.
commonError: Student lists numbers without identifying the pattern or common values.
checkpointTask: After generating lists, ask the student to describe the common multiples or factors.
